editorial.copyrightPolicy: Publisher article text, critic review text, plot synopses and score blurbs are never copied; Swoon'd writes its own explanation and links to the original. No posters, key art, stills, trailers, clips, score audio or dialogue are displayed or hosted.

masteryModel.usefulCompetenceStatement: I can follow and join a conversation about movies: I understand what people mean when they talk about how a film looks, sounds, is cut and is made, place a film and its director in a genre and era, understand how awards season and box office work, and ask honest, interested follow-up questions without pretending to have seen everything.

licensingConstraints.constraint: No film posters, key art, stills or frame grabs. All images are original Swoon'd technique illustrations (license id original-swoond). Titles are text only.
No trailers or clips are embedded, hosted or re-cut; link-out to official channels only, no autoplay.
No film score, soundtrack or dialogue audio. Listening exercises use original or synthesised cues only (original-swoond), with a skip and a text alternative.
Never copy publisher articles, critic review text, plot synopses or aggregator blurbs; explain in Swoon'd words and link.

TMDB API is non-commercial only without a written agreement (attribution notice required, no caching beyond 6 months, no AI/ML use, JustWatch credit for watch providers); OMDb is CC BY-NC; IMDb datasets are non-commercial; Letterboxd API is by request and not granted for recommendation or LLM projects. None are production dependencies before a licence. Wikidata (CC0) and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA) are allowed with attribution.
Studio, distributor, festival and awards logos are trademarks: text-only mentions. Awards names used descriptively; store copy wording pending legal review.
Actor and director names appear as facts only; no likeness, endorsement or fabricated quotes. Public professional record only.
Ratings figures (Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, CinemaScore, IMDb, Letterboxd) belong to their providers: no scraping or mirrored tables; dated hand-verified top-line facts or link-outs only.

safetyConstraints: Sim scenes avoid flashing above 3 Hz and honour reduced motion (cuts instead of sweeps).
Some films discussed contain violence or mature themes: lessons describe at survey depth, teach content-rating literacy, and never push mature titles at a reader of unknown age.
Never suggest or link to unlicensed sources for watching films.
Sensitive film history (racist depictions, the Hays Code era) is taught in plain factual text with context, never gamified.
